items.title: Live: Trump says peace talks could restart in days as US warship turns back Iranian tankers
items.description: The talks come as both the US and Iran continue to impose their own separate restrictions on the flow of vessels in and out of the Strait of Hormuz. Follow live.

items.title: Peace talks, strait closed, China calls out US blockade: What to know today
items.description: One week into the ceasefire, two sets of peace talks have taken place but the only commitment is to talk more.

items.title: Live: Chalmers admits budget won't be as planned but still 'ambitious'
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers says the budget he'll hand down next month is not what he initially planned, due to the Iran war. Follow live.

items.title: Your brain explained: Why it's getting harder to pay attention
items.description: If it feels harder to concentrate than it used to, it's not just you. Scientists say your brain is reacting exactly as it was designed to — but in a very different world.

items.title: Virgin to trim domestic flights ahead of fuel cost rising by up to $40m
items.description: Virgin Australia will slightly reduce domestic flights in the next few months as it faces a hit from fuel costs due to the Iran war.

items.title: What a 'super El Niño' would mean for Australia's weather in 2026
items.description: Australia's weather is expected to shift rapidly thanks to the probable emergence of an incoming El Niño, meaning drought, extreme heat and bushfires are on the way.

items.title: 'Potential is significant': The untapped fuel source already on our shores
items.description: Australia controls less than 20 per cent of our liquid fuel supply and relies on imports for the other 80-plus per cent we need to keep the nation moving. But proponents of biofuels argue it does not need to be this way.

items.title: Prince Harry tries his hand at AFL as Melbourne visit continues
items.description: The Duke of Sussex was joined by Western Bulldogs players at a Movember event in Melbourne's west.

items.title: Bobbing in the ocean, watch recovery team release Artemis II crew from capsule
items.description: New footage shows the moment a recovery crew opens the hatch of Artemis II's Orion capsule and welcomes its crew members home after their mission around the Moon.

items.title: 'Swift tightening' of interest rates may be needed despite IMF recession warning
items.description: The International Monetary Fund paints three economic outlook scenarios that each get progressively worse depending on how long Middle East energy supplies are disrupted.

items.title: Full details of assault allegations against media boss revealed in court recording
items.description: The wife of media head Antony Catalano fled the couple's luxury apartment and flagged down a passing car for help following a sustained attack by her husband that caused hospitalisation, police allege.

items.title: Live: ASX follows Wall Street higher, oil prices sink on hope of further US-Iran peace talks
items.description: The Australian share market has risen in morning trade as global investors bet on the US-Iran war being over within months, despite fuel shortages, higher inflation and a possible economic slowdown. Follow live.

items.title: Collard hearing leaves no winners while queer community further bruised
items.description: Lance Collard is handed a monster suspension after being found guilty of using a homophobic slur in the first AFL disciplinary hearing.

items.title: How The Babadook inspired the 'scariest movie you'll ever hear'
items.description: Filmed in director Ian Tuason's childhood home and based on his own experiences caring for his dying parents, Undertone has become a sleeper hit.

items.title: Quiz: We're going on a trip — don't forget your toothbrush
items.description: What are the pyramids made out of? And which Caribbean island doesn't appear in the Beach Boys song Kokomo?

items.title: Should you turn off your laptop while commuting?
items.description: While modern laptops are good at saving battery life and keeping cool, extended periods in sleep mode could still be putting a strain on them over time.

items.title: Lone backpacker remains on outback station as fuel crisis sees jobs dry up
items.description: From roadhouses to stations, outback workers are losing their jobs as tourists stay away. Skyrocketing fuel prices, as well as concerns around the availability of fuel in remote locations, are causing a 76 per cent loss of revenue for tourist-dependent businesses.

items.title: Reality star left fearing death after fake weight loss jab
items.description: Aisleyne Horgan-Wallace lay on her bed, wincing in pain, convinced she was about to die after injecting herself with a cheap, unregulated weight loss drug.

items.title: Murdered farmer's daughter speaks out as police investigate violent death
items.description: The daughter of a murdered Ouyen farmer says her father had recently made reports to police about sheep thefts from his farm.

items.title: Hidden cameras in change rooms cause regional town hall to postpone events
items.description: An investigation into hidden cameras in change rooms has forced the Horsham Town Hall to postpone events in western Victoria.

items.title: Brothers living in squalor missed multiple health appointments, report finds
items.description: A 48-page report has been released on the interactions between health care workers and two siblings who were discovered living in squalor in May 2020.

items.title: 'She was extraordinary': Famed sculptor Pat Moseley remembered
items.description: Across dusty outback tracks to the promenades of Adelaide, sculptor Pat Moseley turned limestone and bronze into the faces of legends.

items.title: New scheme to allow NSW pharmacists to prescribe contraceptive pill
items.description: Patients will no longer have to visit the doctor to be dispensed the contraceptive pill, under a new pharmacy prescription scheme.

items.title: Trump lashes out at European ally Meloni amid tensions over pope and NATO
items.description: The US president says Giorgia Meloni "does not care" about Iran getting a nuclear weapon, after the Italian PM defended the pope and cancelled a military deal with Israel.

items.title: Gina Rinehart judgment looming in high-stakes battle over mining riches
items.description: Gina Rinehart, the wealthiest person in Australia, expects a judgment to be handed down today in an explosive court battle with the family of her father's former business partner over iron ore royalties.
